title: Prime quotients of a finite field tensor split over a receiving normal field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $E/k$ and $K/k$ be finite-dimensional field extensions [def-pc-field-extension], and let $u:E\hookrightarrow K$ be a $k$-embedding. Assume $K/k$ is normal, meaning that the minimal polynomial over $k$ of every element of $K$ splits as a product of linear factors in $K[T]$. Give $B=E\otimes_k K$ the commutative algebra tensor multiplication $(e\otimes a)(e'\otimes a')=ee'\otimes aa'$ [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] and its $K$-algebra structure $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. The set of prime ideals of $B$ is finite and nonempty. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $B$, the structural map $K\to B/\mathfrak q$ is an isomorphism. More precisely, $\sigma\mapsto\ker(\operatorname{ev}_\sigma)$ is a bijection from the $k$-embeddings $\sigma:E\hookrightarrow K$ to these prime ideals, where $\operatorname{ev}_\sigma:B\to K$ sends $e\otimes a$ to $\sigma(e)a$. In particular all residue fields of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ are canonically isomorphic to $K$ through their structural maps [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-residue-field]. No separability is assumed, and $B$ need not be reduced.

source.place: Theorem B.37, Step 2, printed p.605: all points above the chosen closed source points are rational over a normal extension receiving their residue fields. Algebraic formulation of that input; normality is Stacks Tag 09HM, fields.tex definition-normal.

proof.text: Choose a finite $k$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $E$. The module tensor construction says every element of $B$ is a finite sum of pure tensors. Expanding each first factor in this basis and using the balancing relation gives $e\otimes a=\sum_i(e_i\otimes1)c_i a$ when $e=\sum_i c_i e_i$. Thus the $d$ elements $e_i\otimes1$ span $B$ over $K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian] to this finite-dimensional $K$-algebra, then [lem-sfb-artinian-spectrum-finite]: its set of prime ideals is finite.

For each $k$-embedding $\sigma:E\hookrightarrow K$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] to $\sigma$ and $\mathrm{id}_K$. This gives $\operatorname{ev}_\sigma(e\otimes a)=\sigma(e)a$ and $\operatorname{ev}_\sigma(1\otimes a)=a$. Its kernel is proper, and is prime: if the image of a product is zero, one image is zero since $K$ is a field. In particular $\ker(\operatorname{ev}_u)$ proves nonemptiness.

source.place: Theorem B.37, Step 2, printed p.605; elementary tensor evaluation construction

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak q$ and write $\pi:B\to D=B/\mathfrak q$, $j(a)=\pi(1\otimes a)$ and $v(e)=\pi(e\otimes1)$. Here $D$ is a nonzero domain: properness gives $1\ne0$, and primality says a zero product of classes has a zero factor. The map $j$ is injective, since $j(a)j(a^{-1})=1$ for $a\ne0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] applied to $k\to E$, every $e\in E$ is algebraic. Let $P_e$ be its monic minimal polynomial as in [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. The embedding $u$ gives $P(u(e))=u(P(e))$ for every $P\in k[T]$, so $e$ and $u(e)$ have identical annihilating polynomials and identical minimal polynomial. Normality therefore gives $P_e(T)=\prod_{r=1}^{m}(T-a_r)$ in $K[T]$, with $m\ge1$ (a nonzero constant cannot annihilate $e$). Evaluating in $D$ gives $0=\prod_{r=1}^{m}(v(e)-j(a_r))$. Repeatedly using the domain property yields $v(e)=j(a_r)$ for some $r$.

source.place: definition-minimal-polynomial (Tag 09GM), preceding construction and following characterization; definition-normal (Tag 09HM); algebra.tex lemma-finite-is-integral (Tag 00GK)

proof.text: Every $b\in B$ is a sum $\sum_t e_t\otimes a_t$. By the preceding step choose $c_t\in K$ with $v(e_t)=j(c_t)$. Then $\pi(b)=\sum_t v(e_t)j(a_t)=j(\sum_t c_ta_t)$. Since $\pi$ is onto, $j$ is onto and hence an isomorphism. Define $\sigma_{\mathfrak q}=j^{-1}\circ v:E\to K$. Both maps are $k$-algebra maps, and this map is injective: for nonzero $e$, its image has inverse the image of $e^{-1}$. On pure tensors, $\pi(e\otimes a)=j(\sigma_{\mathfrak q}(e)a)$, so $\pi=j\circ\operatorname{ev}_{\sigma_{\mathfrak q}}$ on all of $B$. Thus $\mathfrak q=\ker(\operatorname{ev}_{\sigma_{\mathfrak q}})$, proving surjectivity of the asserted correspondence and the structural isomorphism $K\xrightarrow{\sim}B/\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Theorem B.37, Step 2, printed p.605; explicit scalar generation in the prime quotient

proof.text: If $\ker(\operatorname{ev}_\sigma)=\ker(\operatorname{ev}_\tau)$, then for every $e\in E$ the element $e\otimes1-1\otimes\sigma(e)$ lies in both kernels. Applying $\operatorname{ev}_\tau$ gives $\tau(e)-\sigma(e)=0$. Hence $\tau=\sigma$, completing the bijection. This uses the displayed evaluation formulas, not an assertion about the number of embeddings.

source.place: Theorem B.37, Step 2, printed p.605; elementary injectivity of the kernel correspondence

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the local ring of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ at $\mathfrak q$ is $B_{\mathfrak q}$ with its actual germ map. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra], its residue field is the fraction field of $D=B/\mathfrak q$ through the quotient map. But step 4 identified $D$ with the field $K$ via $j$. Every nonzero denominator in $D$ is already invertible, so the fraction $x/y$ equals $xy^{-1}$ in $D$; hence $D\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is an isomorphism. Its composite with $j$ is the structural map, proving the claimed canonical $K$-identification. None of these arguments required distinct roots or reducedness of $B$.

Source: Milne iAG2017 B.37 (PDF pp. 616-618) says to take K to be any normal extension into which every κ(g_i) embeds, so that the points above are K-rational; the item is the algebraic form of this. Normality matches Stacks 09HM (fields.tex l.1827), with no separability. The tags 00J6, 00J7, 00KH, 00GK, 09GM, 01HV and 00CT are confirmed in tags/tags. Steps: (1) generation by pure tensors and the balancing relation make B finite over K; then Artinian (lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian) and finite Spec (lem-sfb-artinian-spectrum-finite). (2) ev_σ comes from pushout universal property (2), and its kernel is prime because ev_σ maps onto K. (3) Finite implies integral; only the minimal-polynomial clause of def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension is used; P_e = P_{u(e)} splits over K by normality; the domain property gives v(e) = j(a_r), with repeated roots allowed. The agreement of the k-coefficients under v and j (c⊗1 = 1⊗c) is implicit but elementary. (4) j is surjective hence an isomorphism, and q = ker ev_{σ_q}. (5) Injectivity via e⊗1 − 1⊗σ(e). (6) The stalk is B_q by 01HV, and κ = Frac(B/q) = B/q, giving the canonical K-identification. Edge cases checked: E = k; purely inseparable F_p(t)/F_p(s), where B = K[ε]/(ε^p) has one prime; Q(i), with two primes; Q(∛2), where the statement fails without normality. The DAG grep found no duplicate. No changes.
